key_idea: Shrink the hypergraph by replacing each edge with its minimum fragment outside a random set W, then count pairs (W, T) through Z = W ∪ T. A fixed edge Ŝ ⊆ Z must contain T, which bounds the count by 2^ℓ and shows that large fragments form a cheap cover.
reason: A famous conjecture falls to a short, self-contained argument: an iterative random-set process plus one clean counting lemma. Its key observation, T ⊆ Ŝ, removes all case analysis and explains why spread forces containment. Some bookkeeping remains in the iteration schedule (the varying L_i and the tail estimate), so the score stops just short of a pure book proof.
recognized: Park–Pham, 'A proof of the Kahn–Kalai conjecture' (the minimum-fragment argument)
